lesson.title: Find the whole
lesson.subtitle: P4 pie-chart revision
lesson.objective: Start from one known group of a pie chart, find what one slice stands for and then the whole.
lesson.story: The pie chart sorts pupils into Rice, Noodles and Bread. Every slice stands for the same number of pupils. Only the Noodles group has its number shown.

steps.title: Find one slice
steps.prompt: The Noodles group has 14 pupils. How many pupils does one slice stand for?
hints: Count the slices that Noodles covers.
Share the number in the group equally between its slices.
Noodles covers 2 slices and has 14: work out 14 ÷ 2.

steps.title: Find the whole
steps.prompt: How many pupils are in the whole pie?
hints: Count every slice in the pie.
Each slice stands for the same number, so multiply the number of slices by it.
The pie has 6 slices and each stands for 7: work out 6 × 7.

steps.title: Find another group
steps.prompt: How many pupils are in the Rice group?
hints: Count the slices that Rice covers.
Multiply by the number each slice stands for.
Rice covers 3 slices of 7 each: work out 3 × 7.

steps.title: Explain your thinking
steps.prompt: How can one known group help you find the whole pie?

choices.label: The whole is always twice the known group, whatever its size.
Share its number between its slices, then multiply by all the slices.
Add 1 more to its number for every other group shown in the pie chart.

hints: Think about what one slice stands for.
All the slices stand for the same number.
Once you know one slice, you can find any amount.
Choose the explanation about sharing and then multiplying.
